scenes.line2: How do you prep STAR stories?
scenes.say: Ever freeze when they ask for a story? Let’s make STAR stories your secret weapon.

rows.b: Set the scene in one line
What you did, step by step

scenes.say: STAR stands for Situation, Task, Action, and Result. Start with the context, name your goal, describe what you did, and finish with a number.

scenes.label: Stories
scenes.sub: Five stories can answer almost any behavioral question.
scenes.say: With just five stories, you can answer almost any behavioral question they throw at you.

scenes.title: Automated a manual task
scenes.say: Here’s a quick example. I automated server checks, saving my team ten hours every week. Numbers make your story real.

scenes.question: What’s a common STAR mistake?
scenes.right: Leaving out numbers makes your story forgettable. Always include results with real numbers.
scenes.say: The classic mistake? Forgetting numbers. Always end with a real, measurable result.
